mira: Quick heads-up — saw a weird throughput regression on L40S during a seq-length sweep. Fused-attn variant (fused_v2) drops ~30% at seq=1536 for bsz>=8 vs earlier runs. Pasting a short summary + logs. Anyone seen this pattern?
perf-bot: ALERT: perf-regression detected. Job: fused-attn-v2 | GPU: L40S | seq=1536 | bsz=8 | median token/s -30% vs baseline (last good: 1719720000). :rotating_light:
alex: Can you paste the micro numbers? kernel selector output? Could be falling back to a paged/fallback kernel due to mem estimate.
jordan: short paste from the run:```
model: llama-2-13b
gpu: L40S, driver cuda 12.1
seq sweep: [256,512,1024,1536,2048]
bsz=4 tok/s: 24.6k, 19.1k, 16.0k, 12.8k, 10.1k
bsz=8 tok/s: 24.0k, 18.3k, 12.2k, 8.4k, 6.3k   # big drop at 1536->2048 region
kernel chosen: fused_v2 for seq<=1024, at seq=1536 selector switched to paged_v1 when bsz>=8
mem_est: 20.8GB (threshold 20.0GB) -> paged fallback
notes: warm cache, continuous batching on, pad-to-max off
```
sam: Were these warm (kv cached) runs or cold starts? Also, were sequences variable so batch padding increased effective seq-length?
mira: warm runs. KV hit ratio stable (~0.98). Sequence distribution kept same; we use dynamic batching so some padding occurs but not enough to explain 30% drop. Selector log: `selector@172: chose paged_v1 because estimated_working_set > threshold`
alex: Two quick repros to try: 1) force fused_v2 via env var KERNEL_FORCE=fused_v2 and run seq=1536 bsz=8 (see if selector logic is the culprit), 2) run with prefetch_kv=off to see whether prefetching+memcpy is thrashing. Command:```bash
KERNEL_FORCE=fused_v2 ./run_attention_bench --seq 1536 --bsz 8 --gpu L40S --warm
REDWOOD_PREFETCH_KV=0 ./run_attention_bench --seq 1536 --bsz 8 --gpu L40S
```
jordan: I forced fused_v2 locally and saw OOM at seq=2048 bsz=8 on L40S (but fused_v2 survives 1536 at bsz=8 on my machine). When it doesn't OOM, token/s is slightly better than paged, but memcpy rates spike in profiler (lots of async memcpy back-and-forth).
mira: interesting — selector might be conservative but paged variant might be causing extra kernel launches and serialize KV access under certain stride patterns. Plan: run targeted microbench that isolates attention kernel (no tokenizer/IO), collect nvprof traces, and dump memcpy counts + kernel durations. Also will run A100/H100 to compare.
sam: I can pick up the nvprof trace collection and help correlate memcpy spikes with fallback boundary. Will also run a heatmap across (seq, bsz) and exporter the selector decisions. @mira add ticket with exact config and I'll attach traces. :eyes:
mira: filing ticket now (ENG-ker-sample-423). Attaching quick repro script in ticket. Going to run isolated microbench for L40S + A100/H100, and then try changing `selector.memory_margin` from 0.03 -> 0.01 to see if we avoid paged fallback. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
